## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**Approve — DNA damage at p≈0.70 is justified.** Atlas e6 favours it over the runner-up DNA replication: 7/10 neighbours, the top four all DNA damage, mean similarity 0.762 vs 0.721. Both acquired wells independently show increased nuclear area and integrated DNA (z≈+3.6/+4.1 at 1 µM; +9.9/+4.2 at 10 µM), and the high-dose well shows enlarged mononucleate cells with reduced multinucleation (z=−4.15) and intact actin/tubulin (e2,e4), arguing against Aurora/Eg5 and cytoskeletal MoAs. Budget is exhausted (0 left) and another morphology well would not separate DNA damage from replication stress, so no affordable discriminating step remains.

## Unblinding

Compound: **chlorambucil** (PubChem CID [2708](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/2708))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The call of DNA damage was driven by concordant quantitative signals: massive cell and nuclear enlargement at 10 uM (cell_area z=+12.0, nuc_area z=+9.9 in e2) with increased integrated DNA at both 1 uM and 10 uM (z=+4.1 in e3), plus atlas match of 7/10 DNA damage neighbours in e6. Unblinding to chlorambucil, a curated DNA inhibitor, confirmed this matched alkylator biology (PMID 36714466) and general alkylation-damage repair logic (PMID 15380096).

What was fragile was visual and dose-trend support. The two describe_phenotype calls conflicted on density (lower in e4 vs higher in e5) and e5 raised Aurora kinase inhibitors/DNA replication from only 2 fields, which I correctly down-weighted but could not resolve morphologically. The four dose_response attempts e7-e10 all failed with the same error because I had acquired only 2 wells over 2 doses.

The miss was an acquisition choice: spending the 2-well budget on high plus mid dose without a third well or replicate left no formal trend test and left DNA replication at 0.18 unresolved. With only mononucleate enlargement and intact actin/tubulin to argue against Aurora/Eg5, a third low-dose well would have been more useful than the second failed dose_response queries.

What was right:
- High-dose enlargement with solid mononucleate nuclei (e2: nuc_area z=+9.9, nuc_solidity z=+6.5) plus increased nuc_dna_integrated at 1 uM (z=+4.1 in e3) correctly pointed to G2-like DNA-damage arrest rather than mitotic polyploidy.
- Atlas comparison e6 (7/10 DNA damage, top 4 all DNA damage) correctly outweighed the mid-dose visual suggestion of Aurora in e5.
- Reduced multinucleation and intact cytoskeleton at high dose argued against Aurora/Eg5, consistent with chlorambucil DNA inhibitor annotation on unblinding.

What was wrong or missed:
- Trusted two single-well acquires (e2, e3 with 660 and 542 cells) as dose-concordance without a formal trend; e7-e10 dose_response calls added nothing due to <3 wells.
- Mid-dose visual e5 suggesting Aurora kinase inhibitors/DNA replication misled and conflicted with high-dose visual e4 on density, reflecting field-to-field variability from only 2-4 fields.
- Kept DNA replication at 0.18 and Kinase inhibitors at 0.05 without a discriminating measurement, so p=0.70 overstated separation of DNA damage from replication stress.

Proposed next experiment: Stain for gamma-H2AX foci plus phospho-CHK1/CHK2 and run propidium-iodide flow cytometry for cell-cycle distribution to confirm DNA-damage G2 arrest versus replication stress.
